name: CompTIA SecAI+
outlineVersion: CompTIA SecAI+ CY0-001 V1 Exam Objectives, Document Version 2.0 (copyright 2025); exam launched February 17, 2026

exam.notes: Live since February 17, 2026 (V1, after a 2025 beta). Multiple-choice and performance-based questions. English and Japanese. Delivered via Pearson VUE test centre or online proctoring. No prerequisites. Recommended: 3-4 years in IT including 2+ years hands-on cybersecurity, plus Security+, CySA+, PenTest+ or equivalent. Retirement is estimated about 3 years after launch. Third-party sources report a USD 298 voucher (332 with Retake Assurance), 3-year validity and renewal with 15 CEUs. ISO 17024 accreditation and DoD 8140 mapping are pending.

domains.name: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

objectives.name: Compare and contrast various AI types and techniques used in cybersecurity
bullets: Types of AI: generative AI, machine learning, statistical learning, transformers, deep learning, natural language processing (NLP), large language models (LLMs), small language models (SLMs), generative adversarial networks (GANs)
Model training techniques: model validation, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, epoch, pruning, quantization
Prompt engineering: system prompts, user prompts, one-shot, multi-shot and zero-shot prompting, system roles, templates

objectives.name: Explain the importance of data security in relation to AI
bullets: Data processing: data cleansing, verification, lineage, integrity, provenance, augmentation, balancing

objectives.name: Explain the importance of security throughout the life cycle of AI
bullets: Business use case: alignment with corporate objectives
Human-centric AI design principles: human-in-the-loop, human oversight, human validation

objectives.name: Given a scenario, use AI threat-modeling resources
bullets: OWASP Top 10: LLM Top 10, Machine Learning (ML) Security Top 10
MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems)

objectives.name: Given a set of requirements, implement security controls for AI systems
bullets: Model controls: model evaluation, model guardrails, prompt templates
Gateway controls: prompt firewalls, rate limits, token limits, input quotas (data size, quantity, modality limits), endpoint access controls

objectives.name: Given a scenario, implement appropriate access controls for AI systems
Given a scenario, implement data security controls for AI systems
bullets: Encryption requirements: in transit, at rest, in use
Data safety: data anonymization, data classification labels, data redaction, data masking, data minimization

objectives.name: Given a scenario, implement monitoring and auditing for AI systems
bullets: AI cost monitoring: prompts, storage, response, processing
Auditing for quality and compliance: hallucinations, accuracy, bias and fairness, access

objectives.name: Given a scenario, analyze the evidence of an attack and suggest compensating controls for AI systems
bullets: Attacks: prompt injection; poisoning (model poisoning, data poisoning); jailbreaking; hallucinations; input manipulation; introducing biases; circumventing AI guardrails; manipulating application integrations
Attacks (cont.): model inversion; model theft; AI supply chain attacks; transfer learning attacks; model skewing; output integrity attacks; membership inference
Attacks (cont.): insecure output handling; model denial of service (DoS); sensitive information disclosure; insecure plug-in design; excessive agency; overreliance
Compensating controls: prompt firewalls, model guardrails, access controls, data integrity controls, encryption, prompt templates, rate limiting, least privilege

objectives.name: Given a scenario, use AI-enabled tools to facilitate security tasks
bullets: Tools/applications: IDE plug-ins, browser plug-ins, CLI plug-ins, chatbots, personal assistants, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server
Use cases: signature matching, code quality and linting, vulnerability analysis, automated penetration testing, anomaly detection, pattern recognition
Use cases (cont.): incident management, threat modeling, fraud detection, translation, summarization

objectives.name: Explain how AI enables or enhances attack vectors
bullets: Automated attack generation: attack vector discovery, payloads, malware, honeypot, distributed denial of service (DDoS)

objectives.name: Given a scenario, use AI to automate security tasks
bullets: Change management: AI-assisted approvals, automated deployment/rollback
CI/CD: code scanning, software composition analysis, unit testing, regression testing, model testing, automated deployment/rollback

objectives.name: Explain organizational governance structures that support AI
bullets: Organizational structures: AI Center of Excellence, AI policies and procedures
AI-related roles: data scientist, AI architect, machine learning engineer, platform engineer, MLOps engineer, AI security architect, AI governance engineer, AI risk analyst, AI auditor, data engineer

objectives.name: Explain risks associated with AI
bullets: Responsible AI: fairness, reliability and safety, transparency, privacy and security, explainability, inclusiveness, accountability, consistency, awareness training
Risks: introduction of bias, accidental data leakage, reputational loss, accuracy and performance of the model, intellectual property (IP)-related risks, autonomous systems

objectives.name: Summarize the impact of compliance on business use and development of AI
bullets: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)
Corporate policies: sanctioned vs. unsanctioned, private vs. public models, sensitive data governance

caveats: Domains, weights and every objective sub-bullet come from the official CY0-001 V1 objectives PDF (Version 2.0), read through a training partner's mirror (onlc.com) because comptia.org gates the PDF behind a form. The PDF still says question count and length are TBD. The 60 questions, 60 minutes and 600/900 figures come from the live comptia.org SecAI+ page. Several third-party sites instead claim 90 questions, 165 minutes and 750/900 (and one lists 5 domains). These look wrong, but questions on exam facts should rely on the official page. Price and renewal figures are from third parties and vary by country. Sub-bullets are lightly condensed (e.g. input quotas grouped with data size/quantity/modality). ISO/IEC 42001 and GDPR are added keyTerms; the outline itself says only 'ISO AI standards', and GDPR appears in CompTIA marketing copy.
